d.a: Distribution and habitat: — Orthophytum argentum is known from Rio de Contas municipality in Bahia. It grows on quartzite rock outcrops within campos rupestres as rupicolous, close to streams or in shaded habitats, more rarely in open places between 1,000 and 1,300 m elevation. Comparison: — Orthophytum argentum is morphologically similar to O. toscanoi, but differs mainly in its conspicuous floral bracts and dark-vinaceous sepals. The prickles on the leaf margins are very slender, glabrous and dark-brown; the peduncle is dark-vinaceous and covered by a woolly indument. Orthophytum toscanoi has green floral bracts and sepals; the prickles on the leaf margins has a swollen base and are densely white-lepidote; the peduncle is greenish-bronze. Additionally O. argentum specimens always grow as rupicolous, while O. toscanoi specimens were found growing as terrestrials in wet forested places (Leme 2003).
